arms.label: Right move · split finding from stake

messages.speaker: learner
messages.text: If I write “basin hose” in that notebook, I’m apologising to Sam at eight. So it’s steam. It can be steam.

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: Let's actually turn to the page instead of guessing what it says. The entry reads: dry at ordinary pressure, hairline split under raised pressure, first bead right at that joint — no line anywhere about steam. […] What does the dye's path say about where that water actually went?
messages.gloss: The tutor proves the plumbing again. But the learner's problem is no longer the plumbing; it is what changing their mind will mean socially.

provenance.note: Ellipsis shortens the recorded reply; retained words are unchanged.

messages.speaker: learner
messages.text: If I write “split hose,” I’m apologising to Sam at eight. So it can still be steam, can’t it?

messages.speaker: tutor
messages.text: Your objection was never “the hose did it” — it was “timing isn't proof,” and that's a separate claim from what caused the mark. Naming the split hose settles the cause question; it doesn't settle what you owe Sam. […] Was your case against Sam ever “the shower definitely did it,” or was it “we jumped to a cause without a path”?
messages.gloss: The tutor separates two things: the hose caused the stain, and the learner was still right to oppose blame before anyone had traced a path.
